Drug Levels and Effects > Effects on Lactation and Breastmilk

Thiothixene has caused galactorrhea. Hyperprolactinemia appears to be the cause of the galactorrhea. The hyperprolactinemia is caused by the drug's dopamine-blocking action in the tuberoinfundibular pathway. The prolactin level in a mother with established lactation may not affect her ability to breastfeed.
